title: Pumpkin Hollow
teaser: After the fair, elder Crane was found in the middle of the pumpkin field, and instead of a head there was a carved pumpkin with a candle inside sitting on his shoulders. For a hundred years the Hollow has frightened its children with the tale of the Horseman, only nobody heard hoofbeats, and two lines of footprints lead to the body. Every one of you held a carving knife today.

habits.label: Pulp under the nails
habits.habit: Orange pumpkin pulp under their nails
clues: The door of the bureau in the elder's house has orange smears of raw pumpkin, and Crane carved nothing today: he only judged. The culprit has pumpkin pulp under their nails.
Strands of pumpkin pulp have dried on the covered bridge rail, as if someone held it with an unwashed hand. The culprit has pumpkin pulp under their nails.

habits.label: Candle stubs in the pocket
habits.habit: Candle stubs from the pumpkins in their pocket
clues: A short stub lies by the churchyard gate, its wick soaked in pumpkin juice like the candles from carved pumpkins. The culprit has candle stubs in their pocket.
The pumpkin on the elder's shoulders holds not a whole candle but a stub, and another just like it lies in a furrow of the pumpkin field. The culprit has candle stubs in their pocket.

habits.label: Sackcloth mask
clues: Offcuts of sacking were thrown behind the hay bales at the barn dance, and one has crooked eyeholes cut in it. The culprit wears a sackcloth mask.
In the pumpkin field a coarse sacking thread is caught on a dry vine at exactly face height. The culprit hides their face under a sackcloth mask.

habits.label: Turnip lantern
habits.habit: Carries a lantern made from a hollowed-out turnip
clues: Fresh white shavings of a turnip scooped out with a spoon lie on the boards of the covered bridge. The culprit carries a turnip lantern.
Under a bench in the Dry Sheaf tavern someone found the charred lid of a turnip lantern with stars cut into it. The culprit carries a turnip lantern.

habits.label: Straw in the hair
habits.habit: Straw from the scarecrows stuck in their hair
clues: The scarecrow at the edge of the pumpkin field is dishevelled, and a tuft of the same straw is caught on a button of the elder's coat. The culprit has straw in their hair.
Nobody ever kept scarecrows at the old mill, yet bits of straw tied in knots, like in scarecrows' heads, are scattered on the grain sacks. The culprit has straw in their hair.

habits.label: Prize rosette
habits.habit: A blue rosette from the pumpkin contest on their chest
clues: A blue ribbon with a pin, torn from a prize rosette, lies by the fireplace in the elder's house. The culprit wears a pumpkin contest rosette.
A little paper pumpkin, the kind sewn into the centre of prize rosettes, was found under the floor of the barn dance. The culprit wears a blue prize rosette.

habits.label: Flour on the sleeves
habits.habit: Sleeves white with flour from the mill
clues: The dark counter of the Dry Sheaf tavern has a white stripe of fine flour, as if a sleeve was drawn across the wood. The culprit has flour on their sleeves.
Under the roof of the covered bridge the tarred rail has flour dust wiped along it in a long streak. The culprit has mill flour on their sleeves.

habits.label: Smells of cider
clues: A pewter mug with sour cider dregs at the bottom was left by the well in the churchyard. The culprit smells of cider.
No drink is kept in the elder's house, yet the chair by the bureau smells of apple cider. The culprit smells of cider.

habits.label: Clay pipe
clues: A piece of white clay pipe stem with tooth marks lies on the millstone at the old mill. The culprit smokes a clay pipe.
At the Dry Sheaf people smoke only on the porch, yet under the table by the window there's a fresh heap of tobacco knocked out of a pipe. The culprit smokes a clay pipe.

habits.label: Left-leg limp
clues: One of the two lines of footprints in the pumpkin field is uneven: the left print is deeper and smeared, as if the leg was dragged. The culprit limps on the left leg.
The flour dust on the old mill steps shows the steps: the right foot treads evenly, the left is pulled up each time. The culprit limps on the left leg.

habits.label: Hobnailed boots
clues: The boards of the covered bridge have fresh scratches in a row, the kind hobnails leave. The culprit wears hobnailed boots.
A boot print in the mud by the churchyard gate has neat dots from nail heads. The culprit wears boots studded with big hobnails.

habits.label: Missing little finger
habits.habit: No little finger on their left hand
clues: The dusty lid of a chest in the elder's house has the print of a left palm with four fingers. The culprit has no little finger on their left hand.
The pot boy at the Dry Sheaf remembered cider being paid for with a left hand missing its little finger. The culprit has no little finger on their left hand.

habits.label: Hums psalms
clues: When the fiddle at the barn dance fell silent, a psalm sung under someone's breath came out of the dark by the doors. The culprit hums psalms.
The children hiding behind the scarecrow in the pumpkin field heard a psalm whispered by the body. The culprit hums psalms.

habits.label: Wire-rimmed glasses
clues: A thin wire arm from a pair of glasses glints under the wheel of the old mill. The culprit wears wire-rimmed glasses.
A boy sitting on the churchyard wall saw two round glints from glasses in the dark. The culprit wears wire-rimmed glasses.

habits.label: Raccoon cap
habits.habit: A raccoon-skin cap with a tail
clues: A tuft of grey fur with black stripes is caught on a nail by the door of the Dry Sheaf. The culprit wears a raccoon-skin cap.
A striped raccoon tail torn off a cap hangs from a beam of the covered bridge. The culprit wears a raccoon-skin cap.

habits.label: Smells of tar
clues: The fresh hay at the barn dance has a sticky black stain that smells of tar. The culprit smells of tar.
On the scrubbed floor by the bureau in the elder's house there's a sharp smell of tar, like from greased boots. The culprit smells of tar.

strong: The elder's body was carried from the field's edge to the middle of the pumpkin field and sat upright, yet there are no drag marks. The culprit is physically strong.
The spare millstone by the old mill door was rolled aside, and two people can barely shift it. The culprit is physically strong.
tools: The pumpkin on the elder's shoulders in the pumpkin field is cleanly carved: eyes and teeth cut by a sure hand without a single stray slit. The culprit is handy with tools.
The hinges on the bureau in the elder's house were taken off with a screwdriver and put back, the screws driven tight. The culprit is handy with tools.
keys: The churchyard gate is padlocked at night, yet tonight it was opened with a key and locked again. The culprit had keys.
The covered bridge grille is locked at night, but there are fresh footprints on the far bank, and the lock is intact and untouched. The culprit had keys.
safe: The combination box in the elder's house where Crane kept his IOUs was opened on the first try, and half the IOUs are gone. The culprit knows the safe combination.
The cabinet with the secret lock in the elder's house is locked as it should be, yet Crane's will was taken from it and thrown in the fireplace. The culprit knows the safe combination.
cash: The collection box for the new bell in the churchyard was opened without force, only the silver was taken, and the sum in the collection book has been altered. The culprit had access to money.
The fair's takings were handed to Crane at the Dry Sheaf against a receipt, and now the purse is short by exactly the prize money, and the receipt has been doctored. The culprit had access to money.
medic: The mug Crane drank from at the Dry Sheaf has a bitter herbal sediment at the bottom, just enough to make his legs go weak. The culprit knows about poisons.
An empty phial smelling bitterly of henbane was found under a bench at the barn dance, with a dose mark scratched on the glass. The culprit knows about poisons.
quiet: The boards of the covered bridge creak even under a cat, yet the dog on the far bank didn't bark once. The culprit moves silently.
The dry vines in the pumpkin field crackle at every step, but the children behind the scarecrow heard nothing until the candle in the pumpkin was lit. The culprit moves silently.
passages: Under the old mill there's a boarded-up drain to the river that few remember, and its boards have been taken off. The culprit knows the service passages.
A barrel chute leads from the Dry Sheaf's cellar to the yard, and its steps have fresh soil from the field. The culprit knows the service passages.
sched: Every evening at half past eleven Crane walks round the pumpkin field with a lantern, and that's exactly where he was waited for. The culprit knows the schedule.

The mail coach crosses the covered bridge at twenty past eleven, and the grille is locked right after it: the footprints cross the bridge a couple of minutes before the lock. The culprit knows the schedule.
french: Under the toothy grin of the pumpkin sitting on the elder's shoulders in the pumpkin field, "Adieu" is carved in small letters. The culprit knows French.
"Il doit sa tête", French for "He owes his head", is chalked on the churchyard wall. The culprit knows French.
